propositions: Two identical 106-line CAS push loops exist in YAML workflow and push.py core, each with identical rejection classifier and refspec requirements but diverged implementations across 5 retries vs 3 and final-push handling.
Silent merge-clean-then-exit-loop defect allows commits to remain unpushed after successful merge, converting the disposition from red to silent data loss.

Standing decisions in three files (reconcile-bridge.yml, canary_bridge.py, test_reconcile_bridge_push_retry.py) explicitly forbid collapsing the loops into core; all three decisions must be explicitly overturned.

Strict mode must fail loud on every best-effort return path (non-retriable decline, rebase/merge guards, store-epoch guards, final-push-rejected, write-lock timeout) by raising a catchable exception with git reason and unpushed count, with only the CLI adapter translating to non-zero exit and stderr.

The reconciler workflow commit-back must move into a new core entrypoint that stages+commits dirty trees before pushing, while preserving the exact commit message and author identity from BRIDGE_BOT_NAME/BRIDGE_BOT_EMAIL.
Both workflows must invoke strict-mode push with REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always, and strict mode must immediately reject contradictory configs (sync.push=off or async) without silent no-ops.
